defects.problem: [EXT] The score does not have one unchanging F♯ underneath the theme throughout. The opening upper-register tremolo changes pitch chromatically after its initial F♯; a fixed high F♯ tremolo becomes the later backdrop. Pitch-class presence in every five-second window cannot establish either a continuously held note or its register.
defects.evidence: Opened Lamm/Mutopia promenade-6.ly: upper tremolo changes through E♯, E, D, B, A♯, A, G♯ and other notes before the later repeated F♯ backdrop; the Promenade is largely below it. https://www.mutopiaproject.org/ftp/MussorgskyM/pictures-at-an-exhibition/pictures-at-an-exhibition-lys/promenade-6.ly .
defects.fix: Replace the whole-movement, lower-F♯-pedal account with the score’s actual layout: changing upper tremolo in the opening, and a later high F♯ backdrop/inverted pedal. Do not infer an uninterrupted bass pedal from top pitch-class counts. The 0:58 loudness anchor can remain for a broad later-texture discussion.

defects.problem: [EXT] The claim that the lament ends not on a close but on a fading line misses the explicit B-major tonic conclusion. A quiet dynamic ending is not the absence of harmonic closure.
defects.evidence: The same opened score ends on B–D♯–F♯ chords in both parts, with a fermata: https://www.mutopiaproject.org/ftp/MussorgskyM/pictures-at-an-exhibition/pictures-at-an-exhibition-lys/promenade-6.ly .
defects.fix: Keep the measured final swell and decay, but describe the quiet B-major close rather than denying closure. A broad closing-region cue is sufficient; no note-exact timestamp is needed.
